newsitem.title: GREECE: PENSION FUND MONEY CAN HELP PRIVATISATION - BANKER.
newsitem.headline: PENSION FUND MONEY CAN HELP PRIVATISATION - BANKER.

text.p: Bank of Attica chairman Soulis Apostolopoulos told an Economist conference that dormant pension fund money should be tapped to restructure public sector enterprises as in the case of his bank.
"The productive activation of reserves that lie dormant in many pension funds can serve as a source of capital for the development and restructuring of many state companies," he said.
Such a use would prove beneficial both to the pension funds and their pensioners, he pointed out.
A recent example was Commercial Bank subsidiary Bank of Attica, where Commercial reduced its stake to 20.5 from 70 percent, selling 49.5 percent to two pension funds -- TSMEDE and TPD.
The change in ownership, the result of a three-year business plan, set the stage for a fast-growing bank with high capital adequacy, he said.
Bank of Attica has doubled its branch network, tripled its loan portfolio and launched a mutual fund management subsidiary, he said.
De-nationalisation does not necessarily mean privatisation, Apostolopoulos told the conference.

Selling a stake to the investment public through the Athens stock exchange and hiring professional management committed to a specific business plan can make the change in public sector companies in need of investment funds, he said.
